latin_text: [HARVESTER: from Allen critical translation; source location: Garin edition, Commento 2.22, p. 505]
english_translation: Pico resolves the apparent paradox by declaring that Love is the oldest god, because he existed before the other gods, who, as the Ideas, were to achieve their 'natural' or 'perfected' being only after Love had caused Mind to return to the One and in turn to receive its natural being; in other words, the Ideas were still in Mind imperfectly (secondo il loro essere ideale imperfetto). But he is the youngest and the most beautiful god, because the other gods existed before him, not, as one might have anticipated from Pico's earlier arguments, in their cause, the One, but rather joined to the still unformed substance of Mind in an ideal but imperfect way.
exegesis: [PLACEHOLDER: Pico resolves the Symposium's paradox of Love being both oldest and youngest by reference to angelic Mind's temporal-logical priority. The angelic intellect must desire to perfect the Ideas before they achieve perfection. This represents a sophisticated engagement with Platonic temporality and the distinction between eternity and time. SYNTHESIZER to develop the metaphysical implications.]
kabbalistic_elements: The tension between old and young parallels Kabbalistic doctrine of the simultaneous and eternal emanation of Sefiroth.

other_texts: Plotinus on temporal and eternal causation

notes: HARVESTER context: Sophisticated resolution of the Platonic temporal paradox through the distinction between eternal and temporal causation. Source: Allen, p. 6290-6302; Garin edition, Commento 2.22, p. 505. Kabbalistic density: MODERATE (simultaneous emanation of Sefiroth).
